title: Hungary Walks a Tightrope Between Fiscal Strain and Energy Fragility · 28 Aug
keywords: Hungary, Paks nuclear plant, Danube, energy security, budget deficit, fiscal policy, Magyar Nemzeti Bank, inflation, EU, climate resilience, energy diversification, European Commission
notes: Hungary is confronting twin pressures that expose the limits of its economic stabilization story: a near-shutdown at its only nuclear plant triggered by record-low Danube water levels, and a revised budget deficit target of 7.5 percent of GDP that is testing investor confidence in the new government's finances. Together, the two crises reveal a country attempting to manage a narrow path between physical infrastructure shocks and fiscal credibility. The coming months will determine whether Budapest can hold that line.
